Six Indian tourists, including two women and four men, have gone missing during a trek to Nepal's Shey-Phoksundo Lake, the deepest lake in the country, following heavy snowfall in the Himalayan region, officials confirmed to news agency ANI.The tourists were travelling from Ward Nos. 4 and 8 of Dolpo Buddha Rural Municipality towards the lake when they went missing. They were last reported to be in the Numla Pass and Bagla Pass areas between Ward Nos. 4 and 8 of Shey-Phoksundo Rural Municipality.Local guides suspect that the tourists may have become stranded in the mountains following heavy snowfall, reportedly influenced by Cyclone Arnab developing over the Bay of Bengal.According to local officials, the group continued its journey despite warnings from residents about difficult weather and dangerous conditions along the mountain passes. They are believed to have become trapped in the snow while returning from the high-altitude area.Dolpa chief district officer Junu Hamal confirmed that the tourists were stranded while returning from Dho towards Phoksundo Lake."The tourists became stranded while returning from Dho towards Phoksundo Lake," Hamal said, adding that locals had warned them about the difficult weather and mountain conditions before they proceeded.Shey-Phoksundo Rural Municipality Chairman Dhawa Samduk Gurung said the lack of mobile phone connectivity in the mountain passes had made it difficult to establish contact with the missing tourists."Mobile phone communication is unavailable in the mountain passes between Wards 4 and 8, making it difficult to obtain information about the tourists' whereabouts and current condition," Gurung said.Authorities have initiated efforts to trace the missing tourists, but heavy snowfall and adverse weather conditions have hampered search and rescue operations in the high-altitude region.Dolpa deputy superintendent of police Anil Raj Giri said the six Indian tourists remained uncontactable as per the latest information."Six Indian tourists remain out of contact, according to the latest information," Giri said.He added that authorities had requested the concerned agency to arrange a helicopter to assist in search and rescue operations.A team of the Nepal army has also been deployed to locate the tourists and help with the rescue efforts.The absence of mobile connectivity, thick snow and difficult terrain have made it challenging for rescue teams to establish the group's exact location and assess their condition.According to the District Administration Office, 244 tourists have reached Upper Dolpa. They include 149 Nepali nationals, 44 tourists from SAARC countries and 51 visitors from other foreign countries.Amid the worsening weather conditions, the district administration has urged tourists to avoid risky areas and remain in safe locations.Tourist arrivals in the Shey-Phoksundo Lake region have increased in recent years. Official data show that 4,882 tourists visited Phoksundo Lake during the first 11 months of the fiscal year 2082/83.
Article Summary: Six Indian tourists, including two women and four men, have gone missing during a trek to Nepal's Shey-Phoksundo Lake. The tourists were travelling from Ward Nos. 4 and 8 of Dolpo Buddha Rural Municipality towards the lake when they went missing. They are believed to have become trapped in the snow while returning from the high-altitude area.

Article Title: Dog stranded for 20 days between cliff and raging river rescued in Nepal
Article Text:
Seti was trapped on a narrow stretch of land, with a sheer cliff on one side and an overflowing channel of the river on the other

Trapped for 20 days on a narrow strip of land between a sheer cliff and the raging Budhi Gandaki river in Nepal's Gorkha district, a dog named Seti was finally rescued on Friday evening by two kayakers who braved rain and strong currents to bring it to safety. The rescue followed a three-day effort involving local authorities, animal welfare groups and residents to airlift the animal fell through.Seti belonged to Dayaram Karki of Thado Bharyang in Dharche rural municipality-1 and had been swept away during the Oct 11 flash flood in Budhi Gandaki basin. Seti survived on an isolated patch of land at Jagat Bagar, near the boundary of Chumanubri and Dharche rural municipalities, where residents spotted it last Wednesday.Karki and local youths threw biscuits across the water to feed Seti. The plight of the stranded animal prompted a coordinated rescue effort involving Chumanubri rural municipality, Manaslu Conservation Area Project, Veterinary Hospital and Livestock Services Office in Gorkha, Animal Nepal and Gorkha Jaycees.Tourism entrepreneur and Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP)'s Chumanubri president Dhawa Gyalzen Lama, local Birbal Ghale and rural municipality chairman Nima Lama first explored the possibility of a helicopter rescue, but bad weather and difficulties securing flight permission ruled it out.Animal Nepal then contacted Royal Beach Camp in Dhading, which sent a team of professional kayakers and rafters to Jagat Bagar. Despite persistent drizzle and the river's powerful current, Ram Silwal and Arun Thapaliya crossed the swollen Budhi Gandaki in kayaks to reach Seti. "It was drizzling, and the Budhi Gandaki was raging but they ventured into the swollen river and rescued the dog. I thank them," chairman Nima Lama told Nepalese news portal Setopati.The rescuers placed Seti inside a kayak and carefully ferried it across the river, ending its ordeal. Waiting on the opposite bank, Lama welcomed the team with traditional ceremonial scarves, known as khadas, and placed one around Seti's neck.
Article Summary: Dog named Seti was swept away in a flash flood in Nepal's Gorkha district on October 11. Seti survived on an isolated patch of land at Jagat Bagar, near the boundary of Chumanubri and Dharche rural municipalities. Two kayakers braved rain and strong currents to bring Seti to safety on Friday evening.

Article Title: Wanted preacher Zakir Naik faces backlash for defending Taliban on Afghan girls' education
Article Text:
Zakir Naik said that claims around Afghan women being denied higher education were "wrong and a misinformation".

Who's Zakir Naik

NEW DELHI: Fugitive Islamic preacher Zakir Naik was criticised for defending access to education for women under Afghanistan's Taliban regime, which has notoriously restricted the equal rights of Afghan women.Naik, booked under India's stringent UAPA for terror-linked activities, said: "Everything that comes in the media is not true. The spokesperson of the Taliban said the situation there (in Afghanistan) is not very safe for women."The fugitive preacher said a Taliban ambassador assured him lesser restrictions when "safety is secured"."As far as I checked with the ambassador of the Taliban, they have women's education at all levels till Standard 6. So primary education is there for all females. Only higher education, because the environment is not safe, they are waiting until safety is secured," he said.Zakir Naik said that claims around Afghan women being denied higher education were "wrong and a misinformation"."All the other aspects of Islamic education, whether it be Quran or Sharia or PhD, they even have Sharia teachers. They may not have certain higher education of the Western world.To say that they don't have higher education is wrong. It's misinformation," he said."It is deeply troubling and disappointing to see an Islamic scholar of such global prominence as Dr. Zakir Naik rationalise the Taliban’s systematic exclusion of girls from education. Presenting an indefinite ban as a mere “postponement” and invoking a shortage of female teachers without explaining how that shortage can be addressed is not a credible defence. Such arguments risk legitimising the Taliban’s gender apartheid and lending religious credibility to a grave injustice," said Ziauddin Yousafzai, father of Malala Yousafzai.Mariam Solaimankhil, member of Afghanistan’s parliament in exile, said Zakir Naik should be ashamed, saying "some scholars suddenly lose their ability to reason"."According to Zakir Naik, Afghan girls aren’t banned from education. They’re just waiting for female teachers. The same female teachers the Taliban banned from working? Brilliant logic, Doctor! Apparently, when misogyny wears a turban, some scholars suddenly lose their ability to reason. Zakir Naik you should be ashamed," Solaimankhil said.Zakir Naik, 58, is the founder of the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF). A doctor by profession, he is known for delivering inflammatory lectures in English, unlike many other Islamic preachers who use Urdu or Arabic. He was born on October 18, 1965, to Abdul Karim Naik and Roshan Naik in Mumbai.He attended Kishinchand Chellaram College and then studied medicine at the Topiwala National Medical College, where he obtained a Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery (MBBS). Naik attended South African Islamic preacher Ahmed Deedat's lecture in the late 1980s.
Article Summary: Fugitive Islamic preacher Zakir Naik criticised for defending access to education for women under Afghanistan's Taliban regime. Naik, booked under India's stringent UAPA for terror-linked activities, said: "Everything that comes in the media is not true" He said a Taliban ambassador assured him lesser restrictions when "safety is secured"
